messages.subject: Simulating linear model with INLA
parts:
Dear community, 

At this link, https://www.r-inla.org/download-install, I found that when simulating a linear model with INLA, the precision parameter has to be explicitly determined. 

```
scale = exp(rnorm(n)) 
prec = scale*tau 
y = rnorm(n, mean = eta, sd = 1/sqrt(prec))
```

Why the need of the exponential after extracting the values from the normal distribution as a "scale" object? 

Why precision was calculated as scale = exp(rnorm(n)) and prec = scale*tau. 

Why not using prec = rnorm(n = n, mean = tau, sd = 1)? Why is there a "scale" which is the exponential of normal data?

I also asked the question here: 
https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/570344/simulating-linear-model-with-inla 

Thanks for your help ! 

Bozo
